title: App-Wide Calculator Theme Convergence + Machine Workspace Activation + Release Truth Verification
brief: Bring the canonical PRISM web app onto one calculator-grade design and truth contract, materialize the missing browser/page-sweep execution surfaces, normalize machine intake into shared routed CAD workspaces, activate selector/programming/toolpath authority across machine flows, converge commerce/customer/document/auth/viewer/reporting surfaces onto fail-closed live contracts, and close with benchmark-backed browser truth verification instead of ad hoc manual browsing.
notes: Recovered on 2026-04-10 from the H: drive snapshot by reconciling APPW-MS8 against the live calculator/programming surfaces because the referenced shared sweep markdown artifacts were not present locally. U-APPW41 and U-APPW41B already have active implementation overlap in CalculatorPage, CalculatorProgramWorkbench, CalculatorPage.autoProgramming.test.ts, and src/routes/cam.ts; U-APPW41A now has an extracted shared selector-authority web contract in web/src/features/machine-workspace/selectorAuthorityContract.ts plus active ProgramReleasePage, ToolpathAdvisorPage, ShopProfilePage, downstream routed utility consumers, and a calculator-side JM Die route-authority seam, but broader browser-backed verification and the remaining routed surfaces still need to converge before the unit can close. As of 2026-04-10, JM Die is the canonical PRISM development and test shop, so APPW convergence must treat the JM Die company profile and shop assets on H: as the baseline seed for machine, employee, selector, and print/program flows until explicit multi-company tenancy exists. As of 2026-04-11, Scheduling now uses canonical Haas JM Die sample machine labels so planner handoffs resolve real machine authority into Print to CNC, and Messages now preserves upstream release packet machine and selector truth when inbox follow-up returns to Print to CNC. As of 2026-04-13, APPW synchronization is constrained to direct mounted route contracts until KAR-MS7 app-integration artifacts land on disk; document-learning remains contract-mismatched against current doc routes and viewer closeout remains blocked on a live scene contract. As of 2026-04-13, the shared /page-sweep execution surface is materialized on disk through .claude/commands/page-sweep.md and .claude/helpers/page-sweep.mjs, the browser manifests, machine-CAD sweep, customerDocument.spec.ts, employeeContinuity.spec.ts, and machineWorkspace.spec.ts are all wired through the same shared helper, and the full canonical Playwright page-sweep suite is green at 54/54 across route smoke, machine CAD surfaces, routed machine workspace continuity, purchase handoffs, responsive coverage, role access, customer/document continuity, and employee continuity while benchmark-truth closeout remains the last outstanding browser-verification slice.

purchase_data_policy.failure_posture: If baseline cost, observed improvement, volume, or source timestamp is missing, affected payback/annual ROI metrics must be suppressed and returned with unavailable reason codes.

critical_findings: Browser-backed release tooling is still planned-but-missing; /page-sweep, Playwright config, and manifest files must be built before APPW closeout claims are trustworthy.

Shared machine CAD and print-to-program capability is still calculator-owned rather than routed; the calculator/workbench donor surface now exists, but lathe, wire, and print-to-CNC pages still need the extracted workspace contract.
Commercial, sourcing, inventory, and ROI routes still under-disclose source freshness, provenance, and unavailable-state posture compared with calculator-grade surfaces.
Critical employee/mobile flows still allow live-fallback posture and kiosk-first interaction where phone-first operator loops should fail closed.
Viewer, backplot, and simulation surfaces still retain demo or placeholder escape hatches that are not acceptable as release truth.
recovered_progress: CalculatorPage and CalculatorProgramWorkbench now expose a calculator-owned donor workspace for lathe, wire EDM, and sinker EDM electrode flows, so the machine-workspace donor surface for U-APPW41 is no longer hypothetical.

MachineWorkspaceState.ts, MachineIntakeNormalizer.ts, and MachineWorkspaceShell.tsx now exist, and the routed lathe and wire upload pages mount the shared donor workspace while the permanent routed contract is extracted.

JM Die is now the canonical APPW seed shop, so Shop Profile, Program Release, routed machine workspaces, employee continuity, and print/program surfaces must converge on JM Die-backed master data rather than generic demo org assumptions.

web/src/features/machine-workspace/selectorAuthorityContract.ts now centralizes Program Release route parsing, canonical selector normalization, and Toolpath Advisor machine/material authority derived from the shared Program Release catalog, and both pages surface the shared JM Die-backed release spine instead of maintaining separate local selector heuristics.

web/src/utils/jmDieCalculatorRouteAuthority.ts now gives CalculatorPage the same canonical JM Die release/toolpath selector packet shape used elsewhere, so calculator handoffs into Print to CNC and supported Toolpath Advisor flows stop using calculator-only machine and part-class heuristics while wire EDM stays fail-closed for unsupported routed toolpath posture.

minimum_release_gate.execution_surface_gate: The app may not claim route-complete or browser-complete verification until /page-sweep, the browser manifests, and the surviving route/page census are materialized on disk and wired into the shared command bridge.
minimum_release_gate.route_role_responsive_e2e: All routed pages in the live-generated canonical route/page census must be exercised in a browser-backed suite for shop_floor, lead, hr_manager, and admin on desktop and 768px mobile.
minimum_release_gate.machine_workspace_e2e: Calculator, mill, 5-axis, mill-turn, lathe, wire EDM, and print-to-CNC flows must cover print/CAD upload, 2D/3D review, feature edit, avoid/fill, offsets, draw-from-scratch, and selector-backed programming decisions.
minimum_release_gate.selector_authority_gate: Machine, material, tooling, holder, workholding, CAM/toolpath, and post/programming choices must resolve through one canonical authority contract anywhere the backend already publishes canonical data.
minimum_release_gate.api_contract_gate: Auth, ERP, customer/document, CAD, CAM, turning, EDM, viewer, purchasing, analytics, and machine-live routes must be covered for success, denial, schema drift, timeout/retry, and stale/unavailable behavior.
minimum_release_gate.engine_regression_gate: At least 200 canonical manufacturing scenarios must be engine-backed across mill, 5-axis, lathe, mill-turn/live-tool, swiss, and wire EDM with safety and output-validity assertions.
minimum_release_gate.continuity_gate: At least 20 browser-backed ERP/employee/customer flows must cover login, clock, punch, pause/resume, release, purchasing, document access, portal access, inventory, and message continuity.
minimum_release_gate.benchmark_truth_gate: Prism Auto and benchmark outputs must be validated against internal reference fixtures and competitor/baseline comparisons before APPW closeout can claim optimized real-world readiness.

units.title: Machine Intake Contract Normalization + Shared Routed Machine Workspace
units.description: Normalize lathe, wire, sinker EDM electrode, print-to-CNC, and future mill-class intake payloads into one machine intake contract and promote the calculator-owned CAD/feature-edit stack into routed machine workspaces with upload, 2D/3D, feature edit, avoid/fill, offsets, draw-from-scratch, and electrode packet handoff.
units.notes: Recovered progress from the 2026-04-10 H: drive snapshot: CalculatorPage and CalculatorProgramWorkbench already run calculator-owned lathe, wire EDM, and sinker EDM electrode intake/programming flows, including donor 2D/3D review behavior and sinker-specific packet staging. As of the first APPW41 implementation slice, MachineWorkspaceState.ts, MachineIntakeNormalizer.ts, and MachineWorkspaceShell.tsx exist and the routed lathe and wire upload pages now mount the shared donor surface. Remaining work is to extract the full routed contract into release and downstream machine pages instead of leaving the deepest experience calculator-local. JM Die machine, controller, holder, tooling, material, and print assets are the baseline seed for this routed contract.
exit_criteria: Lathe, wire EDM, sinker EDM electrode, print-to-CNC, and routed mill-class pages share one intake contract for OCR, geometry, dimensions, material, and feature state.
Shared machine workspace can render upload/review, 2D/3D, feature selection/editing, avoid/fill, offsets, and draw-from-scratch across routed pages.

Sinker EDM electrode intake supports scan/print/CAD upload, holder-stack and burn-package feature toggles, spark-gap and wear inputs, and a parseable-source lane that can draft Roku-Roku electrode NC while preserving macro-ready fallback output.

Trilobe macro and legacy-program handling are explicit: the workspace either invokes a live macro/reference bridge or surfaces handoff-only/pending truth until the JM Die Roku-Roku archive at H:\PRISM\JM DIE\ROKU-ROKU is indexed.
Calculator-owned CAD donors are promoted into reusable machine-workspace surfaces instead of remaining page-local.

Routed machine pages still depend on calculator-only state to render CAD/feature editing.

units.title: Canonical Selector Authority + Programming/Toolpath Registry Activation
units.description: Converge machine, material, tooling, holder, workholding, CAM/toolpath, programming, and electrode-package selections onto one canonical authority contract across calculator, routed machine pages, Toolpath Advisor, Program Release, and Shop Profile.
units.notes: Partial overlap exists out of order: CalculatorPage already fetches programming and holder catalog state, ProgramReleasePage carries routed machine/toolholder selection state, and ShopProfilePage owns machine inventory and preference data. The current JM Die convergence slice now projects shared th-jmd-* holder seeds from src/utils/jmDieSelectorCatalog.ts into both Program Release and Calculator through src/utils/calculatorToolHolderCatalog.ts plus the mirrored fallback IDs in web/src/data/calculatorHolderLibrary.ts, and CalculatorPage now defaults VDI single-turret, wire EDM process-package, and sinker electrode flows onto that same calculator-side authority posture. The first shared selectorAuthorityContract is now extracted in web/src/features/machine-workspace/selectorAuthorityContract.ts and actively consumed by ProgramReleasePage plus ToolpathAdvisorPage so route parsing, selector normalization, and machine/material release-spine recommendations stop diverging between those surfaces. Routed lathe and wire upload pages now also derive their shared machine-workspace posture from the same JM Die-backed authority layer, and ShopProfilePage now surfaces the canonical machine/controller registry plus selector seed summaries through a shared web API helper instead of keeping that backend truth hidden. Calculator holder-source messaging now distinguishes when JM Die canonical holder seeds are the active fallback or hybrid posture, reducing one more calculator-specific selector divergence while the broader programming/toolpath contract is still converging. Programming catalog authority is now explicit state instead of note-string sniffing: web/src/utils/jmDieCalculatorProgrammingAuthority.ts stamps badge, summary, posture, and note metadata onto calculatorData programming catalog loads, and CalculatorPage now renders curated or fallback programming posture from that contract so JM Die seeded modes keep their company-specific spine visible even when the backend returns advisory curated packages. The deeper calculator-side toolpath normalization seam is now also extracted into web/src/features/machine-workspace/programmingAuthorityContract.ts, with CalculatorPage public helper exports delegating to that shared contract so routed workspaces and calculator-side tests stop depending on page-local toolpath/license normalization. The parked legacy CalculatorPage normalization block has now been removed, and the heavy calculator coverage suites (matrix, scenario, surface-finish, toolpath-universe, and catalog coverage) now import those programming/toolpath helpers directly from the shared contract instead of from CalculatorPage. A focused web/src/__tests__/programmingAuthorityContract.test.ts suite now protects the direct contract while the broader calculatorData, CalculatorPage, and matrix-style suites validate the calculator-facing compatibility layer. During this same slice, the calculator verification path was reopened by repairing the exFAT-corrupted web/src/data/calculatorProgrammingCatalogSupplements.ts and web/src/utils/calculatorPurchaseRecommendations.ts files and re-exporting the missing shared programming supplement symbols from src/shared/calculatorProgrammingCatalogExtensions.ts, which allowed calculatorData plus CalculatorPage.machineSelection suites to execute again. The latest JM Die route/release convergence step adds web/src/features/machine-workspace/routeProgrammingAuthority.ts so routed machine workspaces and ProgramReleasePage can infer machine-mode programming posture, canonical JM Die seed packages, and default license/toolpath context from the same programming catalog authority seam instead of silently falling back to local page assumptions. MachineWorkspaceState, MachineIntakeNormalizer, MachineWorkspaceShell, LatheUploadPage, WireEdmUploadPage, and ProgramReleasePage now carry or surface that structured programming posture, the focused routeProgrammingAuthority and routeMachineWorkspaceAuthority suites are green, and the full ProgramReleasePage suite is green again after stabilizing fetch isolation for the new programming-authority network path. ToolpathAdvisorPage now also resolves and renders that same shared programming posture from its selected machine axis and release spine instead of staying selector-only, and ShopProfilePage now summarizes JM Die programming authority across mill, lathe, wire EDM, and sinker EDM slices so the canonical company profile exposes programming readiness alongside machine/controller and selector resource truth. Focused ToolpathAdvisorPage and ShopProfilePage suites are now green for this profile/programming convergence step. LatheUploadPage and WireEdmUploadPage now carry the resolved MachineWorkspaceContext forward into LatheWizardPage and WireEdmWizardPage, and the shared web/src/features/machine-workspace/MachineWorkspaceAuthorityCard.tsx keeps the same JM Die machine, controller, selector, and programming posture visible across those wizard surfaces instead of dropping back to a disconnected flow. Focused LatheWizardPage and WireEdmWizardPage suites are green, and the touched upload and wizard pages bundle cleanly for this routed-wizard convergence step. That same routed authority now survives the results handoff too: LatheWizardPage and WireEdmWizardPage submit MachineWorkspaceContext into LatheResultsPage and WireEdmResultsPage, both results surfaces render the shared authority card, and the edit-and-rerun path now preserves the JM Die machine/controller/programming spine back into the wizard route instead of dropping it during results navigation. Focused LatheResultsPage and WireEdmResultsPage suites are green, and the touched results pages bundle cleanly for this routed-results convergence step. SetupSheetPage now joins that same routed authority spine: it hydrates G-code, machine, controller, and part defaults from routed machine workspace context, surfaces the shared JM Die authority card plus controller-mapping note, and lathe and wire results now carry a live handoff into /setup-sheet so downstream setup generation stops resetting to generic page-local assumptions. Focused SetupSheetPage, LatheResultsPage, and WireEdmResultsPage suites are green for that setup-sheet convergence slice, and the touched setup/results pages bundle cleanly. ProveOutWorkflowPage now joins the same downstream spine too: it hydrates routed G-code, controller, part, and machine defaults from MachineWorkspaceContext, renders the shared JM Die authority card plus prove-out controller-mapping note, carries routed machine context into prove-out and air-cut API calls, and lathe plus wire results now offer live handoff into /prove-out so first-article prove-out stops drifting back to a standalone utility posture. Focused ProveOutWorkflowPage, LatheResultsPage, and WireEdmResultsPage suites are green for that prove-out convergence slice, and the touched prove-out/results pages bundle cleanly. ToolOptimizationPage now joins that same routed authority spine with honest scope boundaries: it hydrates routed JM Die authority, accepts lathe-seeded operation and tool rows from the results surface for sequence optimization, and keeps wire EDM fail-closed with an explicit unsupported posture instead of pretending carousel or tool-change optimization applies there. Focused ToolOptimizationPage, LatheResultsPage, and WireEdmResultsPage suites are green for that routed tool-optimization slice, and the touched tool-optimization/results pages bundle cleanly.
